 Aliskerov Faces Cannonier in UFC Qatar Middleweight Clash

 Former UFC middleweight title challenger Jared Cannonier will face rising contender Ikram Aliskerov at UFC Qatar in Doha on Saturday, November 21, 2026. The main-card matchup gives Aliskerov an opportunity to strengthen his position in the division against an experienced opponent with an established record at the highest level.
 Cannonier enters the contest with an 18-10 professional record after consecutive unanimous decision defeats against Michael Page and Christian Leroy Duncan. The 42-year-old American will attempt to end that losing streak against a 33-year-old opponent who holds an 18-2 record and has won his two most recent fights.

 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 According to statistics published by Doc's Sports, Aliskerov averages 5.56 significant strikes per minute with 60 percent accuracy. Cannonier averages 4.25 significant strikes per minute with 49 percent accuracy. The Russian contender also holds advantages in takedown accuracy, recording 68 percent compared with Cannonier's 45 percent.

 Aliskerov has demonstrated his grappling ability through his Combat Sambo background and effective wrestling. He recorded five takedowns against Brunno Ferreira and five against Jun Yong Park, earning unanimous decision victories in both contests, according to the available fight records.
 His latest victory over Ferreira came in June, following another unanimous decision win against Park at UFC 321. Those performances demonstrated his ability to maintain pressure and combine striking with ground control throughout three rounds.
 Despite recognizing Cannonier's physical danger, Aliskerov considers the matchup an important opportunity in his career. Speaking to reporters through a translator during Wednesday's media availability, he explained his familiarity with the American veteran.
 Also Read

 "I followed his career and watched him even before I was in the UFC. I've always liked him, and I've always enjoyed his fights," Aliskerov told reporters.
 The Russian fighter also explained that a meeting between the two had been something he anticipated because of Cannonier's long-standing position among the division's leading competitors.
 "He's been in the top ranks for a long time, so I figured at some point our paths would cross. It wasn't particularly surprising that we're fighting," Aliskerov said.
 Also Read 
 Du Plessis Targets UFC Middleweight Title Return in 2027 
 However, Aliskerov does not consider the veteran an easy opponent. Cannonier previously competed for the middleweight championship and remains recognized for his punching power, physical strength and ability to withstand demanding exchanges.
 "He's definitely the kind of guy who can be unpredictable. I still think he can be dangerous at any moment. I'm definitely going to be cautious and focused," Aliskerov said.
 He believes Cannonier's established fighting approach is unlikely to change significantly, although he remains conscious of the American's durability and experience.
 Also Read 
 Brian Ortega Moves to Lightweight and Challenges UFC Fight Narrative 
 "When it comes to something new, what could they bring that's different at this point? I don't think so. I pretty much see him fighting the same way all the time. He's always tough, always very hard to deal with, always willing to fight until the very end, and he can be dangerous," Aliskerov said.
 Cannonier's recent performance against Christian Leroy Duncan highlighted both his durability and the challenges he faces against younger opponents. Duncan landed 68 significant strikes compared with Cannonier's 15, according to the fight statistics published by Doc's Sports. Cannonier nevertheless recorded five takedowns during that contest.
 Aliskerov also acknowledged the significance of defeating an opponent who has previously challenged for a UFC championship. He views the opportunity as an important milestone beyond simply adding another victory to his professional record.
 Also Read 
 Aleksandre Topuria Faces Santiago Luna at UFC Qatar 
 "This is a former title challenger, and beating somebody like that will definitely be very important to me," Aliskerov said.
 He described the potential victory as something he would remember throughout his career.
 "It will be something I'll look back on after my career. I'll look at him and say that it was wonderful that I got to fight him and beat him," Aliskerov said.
 Also Read 
 Prochazka Faces Undefeated Stirling in UFC Qatar Main Event 
 The middleweight contest is scheduled for the UFC Qatar event in Doha on November 21, with Aliskerov seeking another significant victory and Cannonier attempting to return to winning form.
